examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Determinant of a Block Diagonal or Block Triangular Matrix
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that we have  a block upper triangular matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & e & 4 \\ 0 & h & 8\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & e & 4 \\ 0 & h & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =7\cdot |\begin{aligned}e & 4 \\ h & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =7\cdot 6 \\  & =42\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block lower triangular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A block lower triangular matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and the blocks above the main diagonal contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}]
$$

- $B$ is *not* a block lower triangular matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ and $C$ only."
